tests.statement: At 12.5 weeks the mesh is the sculpt and the 16 body_targets lie within chart spread; a miss is a loop failure, and no chart or sculpt is edited

Movement starts on its own before week 8. At week 8 it is simple sideways bending, about 1 per minute, with arms and legs joining; general movements with all parts appear at about 9 weeks and then hold near 0.35-0.45 per minute through 12 weeks while bending fades, with hand-face contact and jaw opening from about 10 weeks and sucking by 12.6. De Vries 1985 reports general movements as 2% of time at 8 weeks; Lüchinger, with better imaging, finds its criteria met only from 9
Skin responses emerge in the order logged in skin7, first at about 8.5 weeks, from the web and not from an onset table

Motoneuron death by 12.5 weeks: sources disagree. Whole cord, Forger 1987: pyknotic peak about 12-16 weeks, few observations. Lumbar L3-L5, Fidziańska 2002: frequent at 8, very rare at 12, none at 13. Region or method may explain it, so the web must not be tuned to either alone
After handover the learner's map beats shuffled, matched raw, and the same learner with no growth history
From 8 to 12.5 weeks, body sizes follow the Verwoerd-Dikkeboom curves, measured as that paper measured them; widths depend on posture, so they constrain pose and not only size
From week 8 to the end of the embryonic period, whole limb, foot and head sizes stay within O'Rahilly's stage tables and on Blaas's curves; small samples, so a range and not a target

By crown-rump length, trigeminal fibers reach upper cervical levels and grow ahead of the cord as Humphrey reports; maxillary and mandibular skin respond before ophthalmic; the division order in the tract forms from growth, never from skin position. Relay nuclei differentiate caudal to rostral and dorsal to ventral, with the whole chief sensory nucleus at least immature near 62 mm

Ventral horn neurons at 10-12 weeks are immature but fire, some spontaneously: high input resistance, broad spikes, small after-hyperpolarization, moving toward the 13-15 week values. Lumbosacral, in slices at 32 C, so a transfer to brainstem and cervical pools

Human fetal midbrain and pons neurons at 10-17 weeks: capacitance, firing and synaptic currents grow, resting potential and spike threshold move more negative, input resistance and time constant fall. The only human fetal brainstem electrophysiology found, spanning 12.5 weeks; glutamatergic neurons in those regions at 28 C, not trigeminal relays specifically

Order of first appearance in the stem: hypoglossal first, trigeminal motor at stage 17, principal trigeminal afferent at 18, facial motor only at 23, with fibers reaching targets before their nuclei form. The web must reach this order and may not schedule it

The upper brainstem core (Merker 2007) has a place to grow into. By 12.5 weeks LMP (about 10.5 post-conception): the superior colliculus is beginning to laminate with retinal fibers in its superficial layers; midbrain dopamine neurons have projections (7.5 PCW) and have reached the putamen (9 PCW), though the SN, VTA and red nucleus become distinct nuclei only from 15 PCW; striatal D1 and D2 projection neurons and patch compartments are present (7-11 PCW); the dorsal raphe holds serotonin neurons; hypothalamic POMC and TRH appear at GW10 and KISS1 at GW12, with oxytocin and vasopressin later (GW16 transcripts; Yew reports immunoreactivity from 12-14 weeks); the prethalamus is forming the zona incerta, marked as such at 15 PCW. The web must reach their presence as regions by regional identity (S.fate), never by schedule. Their function (target map, selection, motivation) is not a Phase 1 target; it belongs to Merker plan M5 and M6. Not sourced for this age: PAG, midbrain reticular formation

Vestibular end organs are innervated before their hair cells have synapses: peripherin fibres in the sensory epithelia at 8 PCW, fibres reaching the crista hair-cell bases and the first bouton contacts and protocalyx at 11 PCW (about 13 weeks GA). At 12.5 weeks GA the web must not yet supply hair-cell-driven vestibular afferent input (L-048)

Brainstem regions reach their 12.5-week rostrocaudal lengths (midbrain about 5.7-6.0, pons 3.6, medulla 6.1 mm), which set the central path delays SYN_MS + L/v. Animal reference, not a target: mouse midbrain and hindbrain-part volumes at embryonic days 11.5 to 18.5 (Kronman 2024) show how the same regions grow relative to one another; they are kept as printed, with no mapping from mouse day to human week

phase1.learner_home.basis: Subnucleus caudalis, upper cervical cord and lower medulla, is the first part of the spinal trigeminal complex to appear (as stated by Brown 1974, citing Brown 1973), and Humphrey 1952 has fibers ending there by about 9 weeks. The whole chief sensory nucleus is at least immature by 65.5 mm, just after 12.5 weeks' 62 mm. Sources place thalamus and cortex out of reach. No synapses or transmission shown at either site. Müller 2011: spinal trigeminal tract fibres at stage 17 and principal nucleus at 18, but no spinal trigeminal nucleus is described through stage 23, so the nucleus at this home has no source in staged embryos

phase1.skin_surfaces.basis: skin7.maturation above 0 at 12.5 weeks; USER 2026-11-04: only the skin and receptive fields needed at 12.5 weeks

phase1.live_units_by_week.basis: rows times columns of live surfaces in skin7

phase1.start_stage.basis: O'Rahilly and Muller 2010: stage 17 is 6 weeks postfertilization, about 8 menstrual weeks; a central estimate, as stage ages overlap

phase1.limb_split_at_start.basis: Whole limb lengths are sourced at stage 17, segments are not. Humerus share 54% from Wozniak 2006 over O'Rahilly at stage 18; foot share 57% from O'Rahilly's foot over lower limb at stages 17-18; the remainder split in the 12.5 week ratios. Replace if Fig. 7 is read

two_clocks.statement: Short activity windows reduced to a few numbers, then one growth step for all tissues
two_clocks.evidence: A precedent for the form only: Butz 2009 averages firing over 1000 fast steps and updates connectivity once per 100, with both numbers the authors' choices, in a cortical rewiring model. Nothing couples activity to whole-tissue growth. A search also found fast-slow splitting in cardiac and other tissue

equation_adapters.evidence: None; the equations were written separately

sculpt_back_to_embryo.statement: Deforming the 12.5 week sculpt back to 8 week anatomy through matched landmarks
sculpt_back_to_embryo.evidence: None for the method. de Bakker 2016 atlas as a shape source, abstract only, not downloaded, extraction untested

rest_posture_8wk.statement: A rest posture for Body7 at 8 weeks, which it requires before it will build
rest_posture_8wk.evidence: Upper arm at stage 18, hip and knee at stage 19, all approximate; soles facing at 7-8 weeks. Elbow and wrist angles do not apply at stage 17: an elbow is first discernible in stage 18 and differentiated at stage 20, the wrist at stage 21, so the limb rests as one bud with a hand plate. Neck and spine have form only, and body7's own neck table starts at 13.9 degrees at 9 weeks, against about 90 in Thyng 1914; the definitions may differ, unresolved

limbs_at_8wk.statement: Arm, forearm, hand, thigh and leg as separate lengths at stage 17, split from sourced whole limb lengths
limbs_at_8wk.evidence: Whole limbs by O'Rahilly and Muller 2010, 2.8 mm straight on photographs; arm by Verwoerd-Dikkeboom 2010, 4.8 mm traced along the curve to the index finger, near the first age it could be measured, on a curve reaching 38.5 mm at 12.5 weeks. Segments not measured separately

head_width_disagreement.statement: Biparietal diameter at week 8: Blaas 5.93 mm in living embryos used; O'Rahilly's three stage 17 reconstructions give 3.2 to 4.7 mm corrected, mean 3.93, logged
head_width_disagreement.evidence: Verwoerd-Dikkeboom's curve gives 6.03 mm at 56 days, agreeing with Blaas in living embryos. O'Rahilly's reconstructions are the outlier, about a third below at their mean. Their correction factors range from 1.3 to 1.6, and stage 17 spans 53 to 56 menstrual days, ending at Blaas's age, which explains part of the gap. Head circumference: Verwoerd-Dikkeboom 25.8, about 24, and O'Rahilly 18.7 to 23.3, mean 20.5 mm. Corrected earlier: this join had quoted only the largest embryo, 4.7 mm, as O'Rahilly's value

map_before_learning.statement: How much of the map is laid down by fiber order before learning, since the tract already separates ophthalmic from maxillo-mandibular fibers by 22 mm
map_before_learning.evidence: Humphrey 1952 for the order in the tract. Brown 1974 proposes that the dorsal chief sensory nucleus differentiates first and receives V2 and V3, the ventral later and receives V1, which matches the order of first responses, inferred and not traced. So the coarse map may follow timing of arrival and differentiation, not skin position. Kerstjens 2022 offers lineage routing; no source links them. Müller 2011 describes no order of the three divisions in root or tract, at any stage; that is silence in a study not looking for it, and does not contradict Humphrey.

reflex_synapses.statement: Whether the proposed reflex path transmits at about 9 weeks
reflex_synapses.evidence: Humphrey's fixed embryos show anatomy, with behavior taken from other studies, and the path is called probable. His footnote on specialized synapses concerns morphology and says impulses can pass axon to dendrite. Tadros 2015 does not test this level: lumbosacral slices, with dorsal horn recordings mostly failing before 16 weeks, and very small neurons apparently without dendrites there. Tadros cites 8-10 week cultured neurons with the elements for transmission (Hosli, Kim, not read). No electrical recording of trigeminal or upper cervical sensory neurons at this age was found. Müller 2011, 245 embryos by light microscopy, reports no synapses and no fibres ending in the principal nucleus.

sensory_electrical_at_12p5.statement: Electrical properties of sensory relay neurons at the spinal trigeminal level by 12.5 weeks
sensory_electrical_at_12p5.evidence: Nothing at the spinal trigeminal level. Nearest: Wu 2026, human fetal midbrain and pons at 10-17 weeks (test brainstem_electrical), and Tadros 2015, lumbosacral ventral horn. Level not comparable, and Tadros's very small early dorsal horn neurons suggest relays may differ

mouth_opening_arc.statement: Whether the proposed mouth-opening arc, supratrigeminal to posterior trigeminal to digastric, exists and works by 12.5 weeks
mouth_opening_arc.evidence: Brown 1974 suggests it from neuron maturity and reflex timing, without synapses or tracing. Müller 2011 gives the timing it would need: trigeminal motor nucleus at stage 17 and principal afferent at 18, about 8 to 8.5 menstrual weeks, with no stage for fibres reaching muscle

or2010_table1_check.statement: O'Rahilly Table 1 was read through an assistant
or2010_table1_check.evidence: Azkue 2021's independent copy agrees on length and age at 11 stages. Stage 13 reads 4.9 mm from the assistant and 4.96 mm in Azkue; not used by the web's start values. Tables 2 and 3 have no independent copy. Table 2 has an internal check: as-measured x correction factor gives corrected within rounding for all six stage 17 values

motor_death_timing.statement: Whether motoneuron death peaks before or after 12.5 weeks
motor_death_timing.evidence: Forger 1987 puts a peak of pyknotic cells at about 12-16 menstrual weeks across the whole cord, with few observations and a 15 week fetus showing none. Fidziańska 2002 finds lumbar death frequent at 8, very rare at 12 and absent at 13 menstrual weeks, from electron microscopy without counts, and Forger's counts still fall between 11 and 25 weeks. No source compares the two directly. If lumbar timing holds, this loop acts inside the growth window, not after it

movement_source_at_9wk.statement: Whether movement variation at 9 weeks needs input from above the stem
movement_source_at_9wk.evidence: Lüchinger 2008 suggests general movements denote the onset of supraspinal modulation, inferred only from timing with the subplate at 9-10 weeks; nothing was recorded or lesioned. Sources elsewhere place thalamus and cortex out of reach at this age, and anencephaly reports were not read here. So whether stem and cord can produce this variation alone is open, and it bears on the learner's home at the brainstem

upper_core_regions.statement: Regional patterning (L8) to the upper brainstem core regions: colliculus, SN/VTA, hypothalamus, zona incerta, raphe, PAG, midbrain reticular formation, striatum
upper_core_regions.evidence: Onsets only, as test values (upper_core). No growth mechanism: L8 covers motor identity genes only. No first-trimester human source found for PAG or the midbrain reticular formation (searches 2026-11-07; Budinger 2024 and Birtele 2022 midbrain atlases cover ventral midbrain and dopamine lineages only). No free full text for Qu 2006, Freeman 1991 or Yew 1999 (paywalled; Unpaywall 2026-11-07): those values stay abstract-level; Freeman is backed by Birtele 2022, Yew's hypothalamic part by Herb 2023, Qu has no alternate
